title: Supplier Shutdown / Disruption Command
tagline: See the downstream impact of a supplier shutdown before it becomes a missed customer commitment.
painPoint: A supplier shutdown is usually discovered when a shipment doesn't show up — not when there's still time to react.

steps.caption: Incident command, live
steps.talk: This is supply-chain disruption incident response the way it should work: the moment a threat is confirmed, the clock is already running against you.

steps.caption: Loading a real incident
steps.talk: We're loading a realistic incident — the kind that normally triggers an all-hands war room call and a scramble for a status update.

steps.caption: Six engines, one click
steps.talk: Six specialist engines — supplier risk, inventory impact, alternate sourcing, contract exposure, customer impact, remediation — analyze this simultaneously. What normally takes a team an hour of frantic message threads happens here in seconds.

steps.caption: Escalate with full context
steps.talk: Escalating to the strategist — it doesn't start from zero, it inherits everything the engines already found.

steps.caption: Executive approval, one click
steps.talk: One click and this is now on the executive's desk with an approve action ready — so procurement isn't the last to know.

steps.caption: The close
steps.talk: This is the pitch: response measured in seconds, not hours — and a fully documented decision trail for the board and regulators afterward.

cta: TSM turns a supplier shutdown from a fire drill into a pre-briefed executive decision.
